cohort: Preterm pig fetuses, some exposed to intra-amniotic lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and others serving as littermate controls.
finding: Prenatal intra-amniotic inflammation in preterm pigs significantly affected intestinal genes and immune cell infiltration at birth, but these effects were transient and did not markedly impact intestinal structure, function, gene expression, bacterial colonization, or necrotizing enterocolitis sensitivity by day 5.
